name: Anjou

limits: For white wine, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc together: at most 20%
For red wine, Grolleau Noir: at most 20%
For sparkling white wine, Chardonnay: at most 20%
For red wine, Pineau d'Aunis: at most 10%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for white and red, 67 for sparkling white and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

notes: Anjou Blanc ranges from dry to sweet and from light to full bodied, and dry Chenin here tastes of quince and apple.
Anjou Rouge is fruity, with red fruit and a light structure, and is made to drink within three years.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley appellation near the city of Angers, part of the Middle Loire with Saumur and Touraine. Rules allow still white and red wine and sparkling white and rosé. Whites rest mainly on Chenin Blanc and reds on Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, with Grolleau, Gamay and Chardonnay among the other grapes allowed.
